extracted.intended_audience: military lawyers, War Department administrators, and officials who administer or adjudicate U.S. Army/Navy retirement, benefits, and related personnel matters
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of U.S. statutory and decisional rules governing retirement of officers and enlisted men, rights on retirement (pay, allowances, transport, benefits), grounds and procedures for whole retirement, and post-retirement status and restrictions. Intended as a legal reference/digest for applying retirement law and related administrative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailing retired officer to institution in Porto Rico
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer of the Army may be detailed to an institution of learning in Porto Rico where application to that island furthers U.S. military policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 27865, Feb. 15, 1911; importance tied to dissemination of military instruction and policy considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow's six months' pay under May 11, 1908 act (active list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of May 11, 1908 (35 Stat. 108), as amended, authorizes six months' pay to the widow of an officer or enlisted man who dies on the 'active list'; a retired officer assigned to 'active duty' under act of April 21, 1904 is not an officer of the 'active list' within meaning of the May 11, 1908 act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 23760, Aug. 22, 1908. Distinguishes active-list status from retired officers temporarily on duty for purposes of survivor benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quartermaster prohibited from issuing furniture to retired officers under May 11, 1908
rubrics_metrics.description: A Quartermaster may not issue or sell to retired officers, even if they are on active duty, furniture purchased under the terms of the act of May 11, 1908 (35 Stat. 119).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 23623, Oct. 11, 1909. Administrative limitation on use of Quartermaster-purchased property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longevity pay accruals for officers on retired list
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers on the retired list are entitled to longevity pay which had accrued prior to retirement; limitation does not apply to those retired on account of wounds received in battle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 15878, Feb. 9, 1904. Distinguishes ordinary retirement from retirement for wounds in benefit entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of travel to home after retirement for mileage claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If an officer delays journey to his home under the order retiring him until one year and a half after retirement, the claim for mileage may be disapproved because such delayed trip is not within rule of giving mileage when retired to resume residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 2978, Mar., 1897. Emphasizes reasonable promptness after retirement to claim transportation/mileage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mileage and witness fees for retired officers subpoenaed as witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer is entitled to the mileage and witness fees of a civilian witness when subpoenaed as a witness before a general court-martial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for whole retirement: preexisting mental incapacity
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer may be wholly retired for being 'mentally incapacitated for performing the duties of an officer of the Army' where such incapacitation results from natural causes existing prior to entry into service (i.e., not resulting from service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 10820, July 9, 1901; examples of causes provided later in the digest (alcoholism, mental inaptitude predating service, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to full and fair hearing before Army retiring board
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1253 R.S. provides that an officer shall not be wholly retired without a full and fair hearing before an Army retiring board if, upon due summons, he demands it; entitles officer to appear (with counsel if desired), introduce testimony, and cross-examine witnesses including medical members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the officer does not elect to appear when summoned he waives the right to a hearing and cannot properly take exception to a conclusion arrived at in his absence. Cited: R. 23, 626 (Aug. 1867), R. 20, 621 (May 1866), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: One year's pay and allowances on whole retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1275 R.S., an officer wholly retired shall receive, upon retirement, one year's pay and allowances equal to the total of one year's pay and all pecuniary allowances of an officer of his rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: R. 29, 360 (Oct. 1869). Prior suspension from rank and pay at time of retirement does not affect right to receive the full sum. But wholly retired officers are not entitled to change of station allowances of baggage to their homes as other retirements may be.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired officer becomes civilian; no authority to ship goods at public expense
rubrics_metrics.description: When wholly retired, an officer becomes a civilian and there is no authority for shipping his goods to his home at public expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 2071, Feb. 1898; reflects limits on logistical benefits after whole retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of home in a territory and transportation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer upon retirement may designate a city in Porto Rico as his home and thereby be entitled to transportation to that place for his baggage; he is not entitled to a transportation request for sea travel for himself and must pay for sea transportation subject to later reimbursement for actual expenses incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting service toward retirement despite fraudulent reenlistment (enlisted men)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service rendered by a soldier who reenlisted by concealing a prior discharge may count toward retirement if the government continued him in service without trial; the only requisite for retirement under the act of Sept. 30, 1890 is that the soldier shall have rendered and the Government received 30 years' service as an enlisted man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 2022, Jan. 29, 1896 and related cases distinguishing fraudulent enlistment consequences (see II A 1 b/c/d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of desertion or dishonorable discharge on creditable service
rubrics_metrics.description: Service subsequent to a dishonorable discharge may be valid for retirement, but service prior to a dishonorable discharge may not be credited; in some cases fraudulent enlistment without a discharge counts for retirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 27073, 27507 (July & Nov. 1910) and earlier decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forage/wagon masters not 'enlisted' and not eligible for enlisted retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Forage masters and wagon masters employed by Quartermaster General under section 1137 R.S. are not 'enlisted' and therefore not entitled to be retired under existing law (Act of Sept. 30, 1890).

rubrics_metrics.name: War-service double credit rules and territorial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of April 23, 1904 provides double credit for service in China, Cuba, Philippine Islands, Guam, Alaska, and Panama for retirement computation; double credit not given for service rendered in Porto Rico or Hawaii after that date; 'hereafter' fixes operative date April 23, 1904; service in Porto Rico prior to that date counts double, subsequent counted at actual duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 16442, June 11, 1904. Also decisions on when 'actual service' begins (date soldier crosses territorial boundary) and that furloughs do not count as 'actual service' for double credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-island transport service in Philippines counts double
rubrics_metrics.description: Service on an Inter-Island Transport in the Philippine Islands counts double for retirement purposes under May 26, 1900.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Philippine troops not entitled to double credit under statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: A construction permitting service by natives of the Philippine Islands, in the Philippine Islands, to count double for purposes of retirement is not permissible under the relevant statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired enlisted men are not formally discharged and remain subject to Articles of War
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired enlisted men are not formally discharged at retirement; they are pensioners who continue by statute to be subject to the Articles of War and to military orders and discipline consistent with status, but there is no authority for their employment on military duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited: C. 24788, Apr. 17, 1909; other supporting citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-retirement solicitation and prosecution under section 5498 R.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired post quartermaster sergeant who solicited claims by printed circular was not prohibited by statute from assisting in prosecution of those claims, nor was it improper for claimants to turn claims over to him; not criminal under section 5498 R.S. as applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/disciplinary control over retired enlisted men
rubrics_metrics.description: Military control over retired enlisted men, insofar as administrative or disciplinary control is necessary, is vested in the commanding general of the department in which the retired enlisted man resides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired enlisted men may be tried for nonpayment of debts
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired enlisted man may be tried for not paying his debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsistence and commutation for retired soldiers under confinement or en route under guard
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired soldier may be furnished subsistence in kind instead of commutation allowances while in confinement at a military post under military charges, and either subsistence in kind or full commutation while en route under guard to or from the post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission required to reside abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired enlisted man must secure permission of the War Department to reside abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarters on military reservation require revocable license
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired enlisted man may not occupy quarters on a military reservation without a revocable license from the Secretary of War, unless he is employed on the reservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission to Government hospitals and transportation cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired soldiers, as part of the Army, are entitled to admission to the Government Hospital for the Insane, and cost of transporting them and attendants should not be charged against their pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility for Soldiers' Home
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired soldier may not be admitted to the Soldiers' Home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of transportation/subsistence rights by delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to avail oneself of right to transportation and subsistence within a reasonable time after retirement constitutes waiver of that right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping retired pay to correct overpayments or reimburse government funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The pay of a retired soldier may be stopped to make good an overpayment and may be stopped to reimburse post exchange funds or other government funds (company, hospital, bakery, post, regimental funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired enlisted men may accept civil or state employment and hold militia posts absent state disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no statute or War Department regulation preventing a retired enlisted man from accepting office or employment under the U.S. or a State, organizing and drilling a militia company, holding city constable (absent state statute disqualifying), or accepting commissions (e.g., Philippine Scouts), subject to state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment as superintendents of national cemeteries not barred
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'who have been honorably mustered out or discharged from the service of the United States' does not bar retired enlisted men from appointment as superintendents of national cemeteries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired enlisted men may be employed in government departments and receive pay while retaining retired status
rubrics_metrics.description: In absence of contrary legislation, retired enlisted men may be employed in government departments as clerks, messengers, watchmen, etc., receive pay for such employment while retaining positions on retired list and receiving retired pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired enlisted musician may follow profession in civil life
rubrics_metrics.description: Law does not prohibit a retired soldier (musician) from following his profession in civil life because he formerly formed part of a military band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired enlisted man may serve as high-school military instructor or as interpreter for foreign commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired enlisted men may accept employment as instructors in high-school military tactics or as interpreters to foreign commissioners (examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remains of deceased retired soldier not shipped on Government bill of lading
rubrics_metrics.description: The remains of a deceased retired soldier may not be shipped on a Government bill of lading; cost of transportation is not a proper charge against the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment of a retired soldier terminates retirement status
rubrics_metrics.description: The enlistment of a retired soldier operates to terminate his status of retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired enlisted men remain subject to court-martial and may be dishonorably discharged
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlisted man on the retired list is subject to trial by court-martial and to dishonorable discharge by sentence; existing law contemplates they shall remain pensioners unless forfeiting claim by serious misconduct; they cannot be legally discharged by Executive order under fourth Article of War which contemplates active list soldiers only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of retirement order as to promotion/grade changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When an enlisted man is retired (e.g., as a private) the power of the President is exhausted as to that case and the order retiring him cannot be revoked to change retirement grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit for volunteer/Philippine Scouts commissioned service toward enlisted retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Service as a commissioned officer of volunteers or in the Philippine Scouts during the War with Spain in 1898 counts toward retirement of an enlisted man.
